INCONCLUSIVE · CLOCK ESTIMATED, NOT EXTERNALLY VERIFIED

1,573 raw epochs · 7 GPS L5_Q signals · 71.72 seconds of receiver epochs · 9,822 usable IMU samples. 50/72 windows integrated under the selected provisional clock. 9 pass basic phase sample/gap availability. Availability and integration success do not establish detector readiness.

Result: no window supports a conclusive decision under the current one-second full-3D movement check and tested noise assumptions. Inconclusive does not mean the signals were identified as clean.

Flight condition supplied by the user: benign. It is held as an evaluation label and does not select the timing offset or change the measurements. PX4 supplies attitude; this pipeline integrates measured accelerometer data for displacement.

01 / The first constraint

Measurement time and arrival time disagree.

The receiver’s GPS epoch clock advances 71.72 seconds while the recorded arrival clock advances 102.09 seconds. A nearby attitude arrival timestamp cannot repair that delay. The plots compare recorded arrival timing with an epoch-based candidate time axis.

The current mapping is PX4 boot = 1519.086740259 + GPS elapsed + 0.1 seconds. Its anchor comes from the earliest receive-time proxy. Offset status: estimated_from_discovery_only_not_externally_verified. Discovery-only motion consistency can estimate an offset, but does not supply an external timing calibration. The scale is assumed to be one second per second. No offset is marked as verified.

The exploratory check learns one unconstrained phase response per signal from discovery windows and predicts separate holdout windows. Preferred discovery offset: 0.10000000000000053 s; preferred holdout offset: 0.10000000000000053 s. Agreement alone would not establish synchronization; unconstrained response vectors, vibration and timing error can produce misleading fits. This check does not compute the paper’s likelihood ratio.

The ULog’s UTC header can be GPS-derived, so it is excluded. GNSS position is used only for the explicitly authorized fixed geometry origin below; no GNSS-derived displacement or velocity is used. The receive proxy uses the correct sign: paired attitude boot time + carrier arrival time − attitude arrival time.

02 / Independent motion measurements

Supplied attitude. Our displacement integration.

Measured FRD specific force is rotated by the PX4 quaternion, converted from NED to ENU and combined with gravity. Initial position and velocity are zero in each short window. No PX4 fused displacement or gyro attitude estimator is used. FRD offset: [0.02, 0, 0] m, supplied by the user.

Interpolation excludes attitude gaps above 75 ms and reset transitions. The existing integrator also rejects IMU gaps above 1.5 nominal sample intervals; missing samples are not silently filled. Detected attitude reset at PX4 boot: 1584.496462 s.

Supplied PX4 attitude is an estimate and may depend on the flight controller’s aiding configuration. No extra EKF accelerometer-bias estimate is subtracted. Grounded adjacent-sample noise proxy by body axis: [0.2718381817189747, 0.2176027600798034, 0.3242645965757552] m/s². This short ground segment does not calibrate in-flight vibration, coloured noise or attitude uncertainty.

03 / Original observations

Raw phases, with gaps left visible.

Original carrier_* cycles are used. The older moving-mean detrended columns and detection-event logs are excluded. Signal ID 7 is GPS L5_Q here, with wavelength approximately 0.255 m. Each window removes its own quadratic using actual sample times.

Receiver validity, lock time, half-cycle/slip flags and phase uncertainty were not retained. A finite carrier value is an observation, not a certificate of phase continuity. Quadratic residuals include movement, noise and model error.

04 / Reconstructed directions

Where were the satellites?

Fixed origin: 59.3526220° N, 18.0727499° E, 32.744 m ellipsoidal height. The user authorized GNSS position from the ULog only for this location. Orbit propagation uses public NOAA GPS LNAV navigation data; each window uses its own midpoint epoch. Healthy broadcast records are required within two hours of toe, with transmission time no later than the measurement epoch. Transmit-time and Earth-rotation corrections are included.

Satellite directions CSV ↗ · Geometry provenance ↗

Orbit equations: IS-GPS-200N, Table 20-IV. Data archive: NOAA broadcast ephemerides. Carrier frequency: IS-GPS-705J. Nominal phase projections use these ENU directions without a fitted common frame rotation; they are comparisons, not likelihood decisions.

05 / Sensitivity and coverage

Does observed movement exceed plausible white noise?

The same exact integration covariance and conservative motion check used in the synthetic experiments are evaluated at several assumed per-sample accelerometer noise levels. These are sensitivity probes, not calibrated real-flight detection probabilities. Timing, attitude errors and coloured vibration remain outside that white-noise model.

|d|/λ is an upper bound for a single instantaneous unit-direction projection. It is not a predicted phase trace and does not replace nominal satellite geometry.

Conditional quality-screen outcomes at this candidate clock: {'imu_coverage_missing': 21, 'phase_availability_or_gap': 46, 'motion_below_noise_floor': 4, 'px4_attitude_reset': 1}. Windows rejected by the existing movement/noise or gap checks do not reach likelihood fitting.

No conclusive benign/spoofed decision has been made. The current requirements before a defensible replay are:

  • verified measurement clock
  • receiver lock/validity/slip metadata or documented quality policy
  • measured noise model
